NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Platform / Site Reliability Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior platform and site reliability engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Hands-on experience designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure with Terraform, and leading platform initiatives through production. Builds reliable, observable platforms and self-service tools that help product teams deploy and operate services effectively. Experienced in technical leadership, incident management, SLOs and cross-functional work with product leadership.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront); cloud environment design and operation
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane
Platforms and orchestration: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Karpenter
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and automation: Go, Python, Bash, GitHub Actions
Systems: Linux, Puppet, k6

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – Present
- Tech lead for a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters and three regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
- Led development of an internal developer platform used by all 14 product teams, including Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3.
- Reduced the time to take a new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Moved node provisioning to Karpenter, using Spot instances for stateless workloads with interruption handling; reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately GBP 410,000 per year).
- Introduced SLOs, burn-rate alerts and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, aligning the error-budget policy with product leadership. Reduced on-call pages by approximately 60%.
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and later EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code using approximately 40 Terraform modules, with Atlantis for plan and apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Used k6 load testing and launch-day capacity planning to prepare services for major launches. A test simulating 300,000 concurrent players identified a connection-pool limit that was fixed before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes preview-namespace cleanup operator | Open source | 2024
- Built a small Go Kubernetes controller using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; the project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

LEADERSHIP & SPEAKING
- Mentored three engineers transitioning from backend engineering into SRE.
- Speaker at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024: “SLOs that product managers care about”.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)


Dear Corvale Mobility hiring team,

I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role on the Fleet Connectivity team. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and hands-on experience designing and running cloud infrastructure with Terraform.

At Tallybrook, I’m the tech lead for a five-person platform team operating EKS across eight clusters and three regions. I led an internal developer platform adopted by all 14 product teams, helping reduce the time to take a new service to production from about two weeks to under one day. I also introduced SLOs and error budgets with product leadership, and established incident and post-mortem practices. This work has meant turning technical proposals into practical platform capabilities and bringing teams along with the decisions.

Previously, at Brightwater Games, I managed AWS infrastructure through approximately 40 Terraform modules, using Atlantis for pull-request plan and apply workflows. I replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus-based observability stack and used k6 testing and launch-day capacity planning to prepare for major launches. One test simulating 300,000 concurrent players exposed a connection-pool limit that we fixed before launch. That combination of infrastructure engineering, analytical problem-solving and operational preparation is relevant to building a reliable, observable connection between onboard systems and cloud services.

Corvale’s plan to shape the architecture for a new generation of trains and take it through to production particularly appeals to me. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience leading platform work and supporting product teams could contribute to the Fleet Connectivity team.

Best wishes,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well structured. It uses relevant quantified achievements: eight EKS clusters, three regions, 14 product teams, reduced deployment time, Terraform modules, and a 300,000-player load test. The examples demonstrate platform engineering, operational reliability, analytical problem-solving, and stakeholder engagement rather than simply repeating the CV. The main content weakness is that it does not explicitly frame the candidate's work as systems architecture, cloud environment design and operation, or networking/security-related infrastructure work. The final paragraph is also somewhat generic and could connect the candidate's platform experience more directly to Corvale's end-to-end ownership and production-focused engineering model.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is parsing-friendly: it uses plain text, standard paragraph structure, no tables or graphics, and includes strong searchable terms such as AWS, EKS, Terraform, Atlantis, Prometheus, observability, k6, infrastructure, and production. However, it does not contain the exact supported-adjacent terms 'cloud environment design and operation,' 'system design,' 'VPC,' or 'IAM,' even though the candidate's source material supports those areas. It correctly does not claim Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, or train/IoT experience, because those are not present in the candidate information. ATS screening will therefore be strong for Terraform/AWS/platform/reliability requirements but weaker for keyword-filtered requirements involving Terragrunt, networking, mTLS/SSL/TLS, and security.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with hands-on AWS infrastructure, Terraform, platform operation, observability, reliability, technical leadership, analytical thinking, and stakeholder communication. The internal developer platform, service templates, self-service provisioning, and production-readiness examples are relevant to supporting backend developers and taking technical work into production. The candidate's material does not evidence Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, IoT, automotive, or remote-device integration; these are genuine experience gaps rather than cover-letter defects. Systems architecture/design and practical security awareness are only partially demonstrated: the underlying material supports platform design and AWS VPC/IAM exposure, but the letter does not articulate them. The letter shows Linux and AWS/EC2 experience, satisfying the Linux and virtual-machine-adjacent nice-to-have at a reasonable level. It also reflects Corvale's collaborative and ownership-oriented culture through references to product leadership, bringing teams along, and practical platform capabilities.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the second paragraph, immediately after the sentence ending 'bringing teams along with the decisions,' add a sentence that explicitly connects the experience to system design and cloud environment design without claiming unsupported rail or device experience. For example: 'That work involved making system-design decisions about service templates, GitOps workflows, self-service boundaries and the operational standards required to run services in production.' This is supported by the internal developer platform, Argo CD, Crossplane, service templates, and production-operation experience in the candidate material.

2. In the third paragraph, after the sentence about the Terraform modules, add a concise supported networking and cloud-environment detail: 'That work covered AWS cloud infrastructure including VPC and IAM, as well as EC2, ECS and EKS operations.' This improves alignment with cloud environment design and operation and practical infrastructure/security awareness without claiming mTLS, SSL/TLS, or security expertise that is not evidenced.

3. In the third paragraph, revise the final sentence so it does not imply direct onboard-systems experience. Change 'That combination of infrastructure engineering, analytical problem-solving and operational preparation is relevant to building a reliable, observable connection between onboard systems and cloud services.' to 'That combination of infrastructure engineering, analytical problem-solving and operational preparation is relevant to building reliable, observable production connections between distributed systems and cloud services.' This preserves the role relevance while avoiding an unsupported implication of train-to-cloud experience.

4. In the closing paragraph, replace the generic final sentence with a more specific contribution statement using the ad's supported themes: 'I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience leading platform work, supporting backend teams, and taking infrastructure from design through reliable production operation could contribute to Corvale's Fleet Connectivity team.' The candidate's platform, service-template, infrastructure, and production-operation experience supports this wording.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT:
5. If space permits, add one short clause in the second paragraph after the product-leadership sentence: 'I also mentor engineers moving into SRE and have spoken publicly about making SLOs useful to product teams.' This is supported by the candidate's notes and strengthens the clear-communication and stakeholder-engagement evidence. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, IoT, automotive, or remote-device keywords unless the candidate can substantiate that experience.
